items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee (Jimmy Maxwell) does not mention Chu Berry. The interviewer mentions Chu Berry in the context of Ben Webster's playing and a record, but the interviewee only responds to the interviewer's comments about Ben Webster, showing no personal connection or direct interaction with Chu Berry.

ctx.x: I know, but I wonder where the word came from. Earle Warren uses that all of the time.
Yeah, he's the guy that hangs around, the kind that asks 'you where you're going from here'. This lady, for that was and Chu Berry's answer / 'straight up.' (Laughter.)

Well, you know Duke wrote a tune that I heard in Sacramento in 1933, and I still remember, it's the only time I ever heard it, and the words were, 'I don't finance romancers, I don't romance financiers, I just take things slow and easy, dry long so. So finally I asked Cootie that, five years ago I said, this song -- Ivy Anderson, he got very upset. 'That was my song, I sang it.' I said, well, the night I heard it, she sang it. I said, what the hell does 'dry long so', I don't even know how you spell it, even. He…
